title: Prospective, longitudinal observational study of livear health as measured using FibroScan and FIB4-Scores and quality of life (SF12) in healthy adults during self-chosen lifestyle optimization and optimal medical care provided by a medical health coaching business
summary:
What is the objective of the study?
The study aims to investigate how liver health changes under realistic,
everyday conditions as part of a lifestyle improvement program.
The study is conducted as part of a coaching-guided
lifestyle change program that includes improvements in diet, endurance training, and
strength training, as well as optimization of preventive medical therapy and
care. The goal of the study is to demonstrate that adopting a
healthier lifestyle also improves the health of the liver as a central
metabolic organ. In addition, the study aims to investigate whether a
healthier lifestyle also leads to improvements in quality of life.
The overarching goal of the study is to improve medical
care for the population in Germany in the area of prevention.
How does the study work?
As part of the study, a one-time
FibroScan of the liver will be performed during the kick-off weekend of the coaching program, and scores will be calculated based on specific
laboratory values, which can be used to assess liver health. The FibroScan is a well-established, ultrasound-based
method for examining the liver that carries no additional risks; it allows us to
determine the proportion of fat and connective tissue in the liver as indicators of healthy
liver tissue. The scores determined for the study provide us with
additional insight into the health of liver function. These are
calculated from the specific laboratory values. Since these laboratory values are determined as part of the coaching program anyway, no additional blood draw is required. In addition, participants are asked to complete a standardized, short questionnaire with 12 questions about their quality of life at the beginning of their participation in the study.
The FibroScan and laboratory parameters will be re-evaluated after
completion of the lifestyle improvement program, approximately 6 to 12 months later, as part of the
follow-up examination recommended for the coaching program anyway. At the end of the coaching period, you will also be asked to complete the same standardized questionnaire regarding your quality of life.
conditions: Fatty Liver Disease, the Liver Health Score (FIB4), and Quality of Life

interventions.name:

• Measurement of liver stiffness and hepatic steatosis using Fibroscan before and after the
lifestyle modification
• Administration of a quality-of-life questionn

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
For coaching group: being parcipant in the health coaching. Otherwise: interest in participating in the study, no further criteria
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria include overt liver cirrhosis diagnosed during the screening process or
any other acute medical condition requiring treatment, as well as active pregnancy. The
potential participants in the intervention group have actively chosen to participate in the health coaching program and have and wish to implement them; the only
additional inclusion criterion is an interest in participating in the study. The same applies to the control group;
these are individuals with an intrinsic interest in improving their health.
Exclusion criteria include overt liver cirrhosis or any other medical condition requiring urgent treatment, or active pregnancy; the inclusion criterion is an interest in  participating in the study.
